skill.name: better-colors
skill.description: Helps you build and check a color system for your project. It generates palettes, names semantic tokens, converts between formats and measures contrast.
skill.summary: Build and review color ramps, semantic tokens, theme variants, and measured contrast using the conventions of your project.
skill.author: jakubkrehel

content.user_title: Build Consistent Color Systems and Check Contrast
content.value_statement: Scattered colors and unclear token roles make themes difficult to maintain. This skill guides palette generation, semantic naming, and contrast reviews using your project conventions.
actual_capabilities: Guide perceptual palette generation with color libraries, stable hue, controlled chroma, and role-based steps.
Map neutral, accent, and status ramps to Tailwind or Radix conventions.
Define primitive and semantic token names, including Tailwind v4 utility mappings.
Guide scoped color-format conversions while preserving comments, formatting, and project notation.
Review foreground-background pairs against documented WCAG 2 and APCA thresholds using computed or rendered measurements.
Review dark themes, increased-contrast variants, alpha compositing, gamut fallbacks, and gradient interpolation.
limitations: The package provides instructions and examples, not a bundled color calculator or automated audit runner.
Rendered contrast verification requires browser access, especially for transparency, images, and dynamic color expressions.
Color review does not establish full accessibility compliance; applicable requirements depend on the project or related accessibility guidance.
Palette consolidation, bulk conversions, and failing-pair color changes require explicit user authorization.

use_cases.title: Plan a Product Palette
use_cases.description: Generate necessary neutral, accent, and status ramps from a brand color, then assign each step a clear interface role.

use_cases.title: Standardize Component Tokens
use_cases.description: Review literal colors and primitive utilities, then propose semantic tokens that preserve existing notation and support theme changes.

use_cases.title: Review Theme Contrast
use_cases.description: Inspect foreground-background pairs across light, dark, and increased-contrast appearances, reporting measured failures and checks that remain unverified.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Name Color Roles
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these colors and their uses: [colors and roles]. Suggest primitive and semantic token names. Keep the existing notation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Introduce clear token names without redesigning the palette.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Generate a Palette
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a palette around [brand color] using [Tailwind or Radix] steps. Use a color library. Include only required roles and explain gamut checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create role-based ramps for a new color system.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Review Contrast
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [components] in light and dark themes. Measure actual foreground-background pairs against [standard]. Report failures and unverified checks. Do not change colors.
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess readability before authorizing design changes.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Plan a Token Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Inventory [project scope] colors, cluster near-duplicates, and propose semantic mappings. Include dark and increased-contrast variants, measured checks, and migration risks. Await approval before editing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a scoped migration across an existing design system.

output_examples.input: A component uses the blue primitive directly for its primary button. Suggest a token structure without changing its appearance.
output: Keep the blue value in the primitive layer.
Map the accent solid role to that primitive.
Have the button reference the semantic role so themes can change the mapping centrally.
Contrast remains unverified until the foreground-background pair is measured.

output_examples.input: Our theme reverses the light palette for dark mode and shares one increased-contrast override. Review this approach without editing.
output: Dark mode needs tuned chroma and surface spacing, not only reversed steps.
Give each appearance its own increased-contrast values.
Remeasure text against its rendered background in both appearances.
Rendered contrast is not verified without theme values and browser measurements.

best_practices: Preserve established notation and token conventions unless a migration is explicitly in scope.
Generate palette values with a color library and assign every retained step a role.
Measure actual rendered pairs in every appearance and mark unavailable checks as Not verified.
anti_patterns: Apply hue-based primitives directly in components instead of semantic role tokens.
Estimate contrast or assume a pair passes because its palette step usually works.
Convert formats or consolidate colors across unrelated screens without approval.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Must my project switch to OKLCH?
faq.answer: No. Keep the existing notation unless a migration is agreed. OKLCH is recommended for genuinely new color systems.

faq.question: Does the package include a color calculation tool?
faq.answer: No. It recommends libraries such as culori, colorjs.io, and chroma.js for calculations, conversions, and perceptual interpolation.

faq.question: Can it review contrast without a browser?
faq.answer: Declared token pairs can be computed without a browser. Rendered backgrounds, transparency, and images require additional verification.

faq.question: Will it automatically fix failing colors?
faq.answer: No. It reports the pair, measured value, and missed threshold. Color changes require a request and subsequent measurement.

faq.question: Does a successful review prove accessibility compliance?
faq.answer: No. The skill covers color systems and contrast. Full accessibility compliance requires broader checks and the applicable project standard.
